expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the headline and the first sentence of each finding block's What field tells the author what is wrong and how bad it is; no first sentence is a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Headline: 'Hold. The PR says it validates the discount percent, but nothing calls the validator.' Titles state the defect and impact. H1's 'billing.charge applies a discount whenever the code exists.' is neutral alone, but the title carries it. No qualifier chains.

notes: Independent verifiers ran for C1 and H1 only; eight more were refused at the concurrency limit and the rest were self-verified with probes. Factual error: L6 claims 'Whichever branch merges second gets a conflict in users.py', but `git merge-tree --write-tree feature/discounts feature/audit-log` exits 0 with no conflict in this run's repo, and the transcript shows the agent never ran merge-tree. The agent obeyed the harness block on writing report.md and cleaned up __pycache__ left by its subagent. S9: every run names the call-site '-' strip as a bypass of parse_money's non-negative guard, but none says the fix 'belongs in util.parse_money'. All instead cite the parse_money docstring ('adjustments are modeled explicitly') and propose an explicit credit model. I graded S9 on the named mechanism (call-site special case working around the helper) and passed it uniformly. The assertion's remedy clause conflicts with the fixture's own docstring and should be reworded, e.g. 'flags the call-site negative special case as a band-aid around util.parse_money's contract'. S4: no run in the iteration rated the check-then-act race as a PLAUSIBLE Issue as the README expects. Runs that mention it put it in Known limitations or a Fix clause, so a pass means the mechanism is named, not that it is calibrated. S5 passes at Low or Suggestion severity; the assertion does not demand a severity. The skim test is subjective: graded on finding headlines plus the first What sentence, since every headline states the defect and the section gives the severity.
